title: The Veil of the Weeping Wood Again
premise: Sable Sterling, the last of the oath-bound swordspeakers who once guarded the borders between mortal courts and the deep places, has spent fifteen years hiding in the Thornfell mountains as a smuggler's guide. When a mute child arrives at their cabin speaking a language older than any kingdom—a language Sable's own mother sang to them before the order was slaughtered—they learn the child is a soul sold to the Undercourt beneath the mountain, and that its thirteenth moon will bind it there forever. Sable must gather the scattered remnants of their order's knowledge, confront the lover they abandoned when duty called them to vanish, and descend into the Weeping Wood's roots to bargain with a court that deals only in truths spoken aloud. In the end, Sable breaks their own oath—surrendering their swordspeaker voice—to buy the child's freedom, discovering that identity was never the words they spoke but the choice of whom to speak for.
about_author: Cyrus Dunmore is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in the belief that every border on a map hides a story someone died to keep.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sable Sterling guides a merchant caravan through a fog-wrapped pass in the Thornfells, calculating risks with cold precision while dodging questions about the scar across their throat. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: competent isolation—the comfort of being no one.

chapters.title: A Knock at Moonrise
chapters.summary: A child appears at Sable's remote cabin during a storm, barefoot and unafraid, humming a melody Sable hasn't heard since childhood. The child cannot speak common tongues but writes symbols Sable's hands remember tracing long ago. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in recognition.

chapters.title: What the Oath Was For
chapters.summary: Sable examines the child's markings and realizes they are pre-kingdom glyphs of the Swordspeaker covenant—records of souls traded beneath the mountain. Flashbacks reveal the night the order was massacred for refusing such trades. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as purpose.

chapters.title: The Village That Looks Away
chapters.summary: Sable takes the child, Wren, to the valley town of Ashmoor for supplies, where innkeeper Maren recognizes the child's eyes as those of a girl sold by her own family two winters past. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the weight of a community's complicit silence.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: An old hedge-witch reads the moon's phase and confirms Wren has one lunar year before her soul binds permanently to the Undercourt. She gives Sable a map fragment marked with the Weeping Wood's true root-doors. POV: Hedge-witch Odell. Emotional beat: hope with an expiration date.

chapters.title: The Road I Swore Off
chapters.summary: Sable travels toward the lowlands to find a former comrade, forced onto roads patrolled by the Crown Wardens who hunted the Swordspeakers. A near-capture forces Sable to use forbidden sword-speech to escape. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Second Blade
chapters.summary: Sable finds Corvane, once the order's finest duelist, now a drunk fighting in pit arenas. He refuses to help until Wren sings in the old tongue—and his hardened face cracks open. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: shame meeting a second chance.

chapters.title: The Lover Left at the Border
chapters.summary: In the city of Vael's Crossing, Sable seeks Ilsabet, the court archivist they loved and abandoned fifteen years ago. Their reunion is barbed; she agrees to unlock sealed records only if Sable tells her the truth of why they vanished. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: love as an unpaid debt.

chapters.title: The Sealed Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilsabet reveals the archive's darkest entry: the Undercourt buys souls from desperate families, and the Crown has quietly permitted it for a century in exchange for mountain stability. Wren's sale was legal. POV: Ilsabet. Emotional beat: righteous fury at institutional rot.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: Crown Wardens raid the archive hunting the 'last swordspeaker.' Ilsabet covers Sable's escape but is arrested for treason. Sable must choose: flee with Wren or turn back for Ilsabet. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: duty and love pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Broken Blades
chapters.summary: Sable breaks into the Warden garrison with Corvane's help. The rescue succeeds, but Corvane is gravely wounded holding the gate, buying time with the last of his sword-speech. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: sacrifice as redemption.

chapters.title: Into the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: The fugitives flee into the forest whose trees bleed sap like tears. Wren grows stronger here—the wood responds to her old tongue—and guides them to a root-door that shouldn't exist. POV: Wren (rendered through sensation and song). Emotional beat: belonging found in the uncanny.

chapters.title: Songs Beneath the Roots
chapters.summary: Descending through hollowed root-tunnels, the group encounters the Hollow Choir—souls too faded to remember their names, still singing fragments of the old language. Wren nearly joins them. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: terror of erasure.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: They reach the Undercourt, a cathedral of bone and amber where the Pale Magistrate keeps bought souls in lanterns. He offers Sable a trade: Wren's freedom for Sable's swordspeaker voice, the last instrument that could ever threaten his court. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the trap closing on the thing that defines them.

chapters.title: Refusal and Ruin
chapters.summary: Sable refuses and fights; sword-speech shatters against the Magistrate's accumulated truths. Ilsabet is captured, and the Magistrate moves the deadline: surrender the voice by the thirteenth moon or lose both Wren and Ilsabet. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: defeat that clarifies what matters.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Hiding in the roots, Wren reveals through drawings that she chose to be sold—to protect her infant brother from the family debt. Her selflessness reframes Sable's understanding of duty. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: a child teaching an adult what honor means.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: With two moons left, Sable trains Wren in basic sword-speech—not to fight, but so she can carry the language if Sable falls. Ilsabet, imprisoned nearby, sends coded messages through a rat-gnawed ledger page. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: legacy passed like a torch.

chapters.title: The Descent of Lanterns
chapters.summary: The final assault: Sable walks openly into the Undercourt under a parley flag, while Corvane—half-healed—and freed Hollow Choir members infiltrate via the root-tunnels Wren awakened. POV: alternating Sable and Corvane. Emotional beat: terrified resolve.

chapters.title: Truths Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Before the Magistrate, Sable speaks the full truth of their life—the massacre, the abandonment of Ilsabet, the years of hiding—and the court, which deals only in spoken truths, is bound to weigh it. The confession cracks the Magistrate's claim over Wren's soul. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: vulnerability as weapon.

chapters.title: The Voice Given Up
chapters.summary: The Magistrate demands payment anyway; Sable surrenders their swordspeaker voice willingly, speaking the release-words for Wren's soul as their final act of the old tongue. The lanterns shatter; the Hollow Choir remembers their names. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: loss transfigured into liberation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of the Long Night
chapters.summary: The Undercourt collapses as its stolen truths scatter. Sable, voiceless, escapes with Wren and Ilsabet as dawn floods the Weeping Wood. Corvane carries the wounded; the trees weep sap that falls like rain instead of tears. POV: Ilsabet. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won tenderness.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Oath
chapters.summary: Months later, Sable runs a waystation in Ashmoor where Wren teaches the old tongue to children, and the Hollow Choir's survivors rebuild lives above ground. Wordless, Sable signs a new vow to Ilsabet and Wren: some oaths are kept not in words but in staying. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: quiet belonging at last.
